The '''2025–26 BYU Cougars men's basketball team''' represented [[Brigham Young University]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cougars were led by second-year head coach [[Kevin Young (basketball, born 1981)|Kevin Young]] and play their home games at [[Marriott Center]] in [[Provo, Utah]] as third-year members of the [[Big 12 Conference]].

==Previous season==
The [[2024–25 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|Cougars]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] 26–10, 14–6 in [[2024–25 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to finish in a tie for third place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]], they defeated [[2024–25 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] in the Quarterfinals before losing to [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the semifinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=BYU weathers the storm again in 96-92 quarterfinal win over No. 12 Iowa State |url=https://byucougars.com/news/2025/03/13/byu-weathers-the-storm-again-in-96-92-quarterfinal-win-over-no-12-iowa-state}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=No. 17 BYU falls to No. 2 Houston in semifinals of Phillips 66 Big 12 Championship |url=https://byucougars.com/news/2025/03/14/no-17-byu-falls-to-no-2-houston-in-semifinals-of-phillips-66-big-12-championship}}</ref> They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 6 seed in the East region. The Cougars defeated [[2024–25 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in the first round, 80−71.<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 17 BYU defeats VCU 80-71 in first round of NCAA Tournament |url=https://byucougars.com/news/2025/03/20/mbb-vs-vcu}}</ref> In the second round they defeated [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], 91−89.<ref>{{cite web |title=Saunders leads BYU to 91-89 win over Wisconsin, on to Sweet Sixteen |url=https://byucougars.com/news/2025/03/22/saunders-leads-byu-to-91-89-win-over-wisconsin-on-to-sweet-sixteen}}</ref> BYU lost in the sweet sixteen to [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], 113−88.<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 17 BYU ends season with loss to No. 7 Alabama in NCAA Sweet 16 |url=https://byucougars.com/news/2025/03/27/no-17-byu-seasons-ends-with-loss-to-no-7-alabama-in-ncaa-sweet-16}}</ref>

==Awards==
Three BYU players received All-Big 12 awards for the season. AJ Dybantsa was named to the All-Big 12 First Team and recognized as the conference's Freshman of the Year, while Richie Saunders and Rob Wright were named to the Second and Third Teams, respectively.<ref>{{cite web |title=2026 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men’s Basketball Awards Unveiled |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2026/3/9/2026-phillips-66-all-big-12-mens-basketball-awards-unveiled.aspx |access-date=10 March 2026}}</ref> Dybantsa was also named a [[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus All-American]].
